title: Online safety
examples: What should I do if a stranger asks me for my password online?
Is it okay to share my school name on social media?
Who should I tell if someone makes me feel uncomfortable online?

explain.say: Today we are learning about staying safe online.

items: Be careful with people you do not know.
Tell a trusted adult if something feels wrong.

explain.say: First we talk about keeping your privacy safe online.
Never share things like your full address or phone number online.
Next we learn about being careful with strangers online.
If a stranger asks you to meet them, say no right away.
Finally, if something worries you, you must report it.

faq.q: What if a friend asks me for my password?
faq.a: You should never share your passwords with anyone online. Only you should know your secret passwords.
asks: Can I tell my best friend my password?
Is it okay to share my login details?

faq.q: How do I know if someone online is a stranger?
faq.a: If you do not know them from school or family, they are a stranger online. You should treat them with caution.
asks: Are people online always real people?
What is the difference between a friend and a stranger online?

faq.q: What does it mean to report something online?
faq.a: Reporting means telling a responsible adult or the website staff about something bad. This helps keep everyone safe.
asks: Who do I report things to?
If something is mean online, what should I do?

faq.q: Can I share pictures of my pet online?
faq.a: You can share pictures of your pet, but never include your home address in the photo or caption. Keep location private.
asks: Can I post pictures of my house?

faq.q: If a stranger sends me a gift online, what should I do?
faq.a: Do not accept any gifts, money, or messages from strangers. Always show these things to a trusted adult first.
asks: Should I open packages from online friends?
What if a stranger promises me something nice?

facts: Never share your passwords with anyone online.
If someone online makes you feel uncomfortable, tell a trusted adult.
Personal details like your address are private information.
If you meet someone online, always tell a parent or guardian.

quiz.say: You are talking to someone online you do not know. This person is a:
quiz.why: You should be careful with people you do not know from real life.

wrong.1: A friend is someone you actually know and trust.
wrong.2: A teacher is someone at your school who knows you.
wrong.3: A family member is someone who lives with you.

quiz.say: Which of these is okay to share online?
quiz.why: Your favourite colour is just a fun fact and does not give away where you live.

wrong.0: Your phone number is private information that should stay secret.
wrong.1: Your street address tells people exactly where your house is.
wrong.3: Your school name can help strangers find you.

quiz.say: If something online makes you feel scared, what is the best first step?

options.show: Ignore it and hope it stops
options.say: Ignore it and hope it stops

quiz.why: Telling an adult is the safest way to handle worries online.

wrong.0: Ignoring it might let the bad thing keep happening.
wrong.1: Replying might make the person keep talking to you.
wrong.2: Deleting might remove important evidence you need to show an adult.
